the new set of higher order boundary layer equations, with a turbulence model, is a powerful tool for the prediction of the local and integral characteristics of the attached turbulent boundary layer along strongly curved surfaces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the zero-equation model for the turbulent kinetic energy is not adequate to simulate the turbulent boundary layer along strongly curved surfaces.

the use of the higher-order boundary-layer equation with zero-equation eddy-viscosity model provides a more accurate prediction for the mean velocity profile and skin friction than the use of the conventional boundary-layer equation with a zero-equation edd-viscosity model.
